note: Set B's seven claims are all faithful and well-bound: the solar thermal collector's type, location, hot-water function and electric-coil supplemental heat (with the 'when required' condition kept), plus the control system's monitoring/metering functions and remote control of lighting and mechanical systems. Set A largely repeats the same 22% California lighting statistic three times, and one of those claims has a garbled quote ('ME onsumes...') with an unreadable entity 'ME', while another restates 'electrical use' as 'energy consumption'. Set A does capture the passive-design envelope and collector type/location, but its redundancy and the misread claim make it weaker overall.
